findings.problem: "Neither weak nor low in caffeine" goes too far. The caffeine lesson says white sits anywhere across the spread; only a bud-heavy white can beat a black.
findings.change: Now "it is not weak, nor dependably low in caffeine".

findings.problem: No step put the water on the leaf.
findings.change: Now begins "Pour the water on and steep 3 to 5 minutes".

findings.problem: The stem ended "oxidises lightly across a long wither", which ruled out the option "Withering" for free.
findings.change: Stem now: "Which processing step does white tea skip, so that it oxidises lightly before drying?"

findings.problem: The right answer was the longest option (42 characters against 34).
findings.change: Two wrong options lengthened: "The long wither drives off most caffeine" and "A pale liquor means less caffeine than black".
